claims.claim: minimum-sufficient-v2 is the single prospective policy; historical minimum-sufficient-v1 artifacts remain readable.

Runtime uses one deterministic derivation boundary consuming authored requirements, exact subjects, committed deltas, correction scope, failed observations and bound evidence, retaining broader requirements when narrowing is unproven.
Canonical failure reports preserve exact nodeid and phase separately from display limits, bind profile/toolchain/fingerprint material, and fail closed on incomplete or excessive material.

Attribution requires exact comparable subjects and conditions: PASS/FAIL identifies candidate regression, equivalent FAIL/FAIL identifies baseline failure, and unmatched or divergent observations remain UNRESOLVED.
Evidence reuse validates subject, command, profile, toolchain, tree, delta, failure-set and raw-content bindings, with separate REUSED and EXECUTED audit records.

Correction probes remain within authorized scope and retain authored integration requirements. Raw exits remain unchanged; nonzero outcomes are nonblocking only when every observed failure is proven PRE_EXISTING_BASELINE.

Regression coverage includes failure populations, attribution counterexamples, reuse invalidation, fallback, scope isolation and raw exits. The repaired supersession fixture now records its exact candidate delta while preserving current-revision READY and stale-selector rejection. The fixture defect reproduced on both the failed candidate and exact TASK-317 base; the corrected node passed locally.
V2 remains within deterministic verification authority. This repair changes only the supersession fixture, preserves production admission, and leaves frozen RUN-316-002 lineage untouched.
